problem: University students struggle to find compatible study partners and groups, leading to inefficient study sessions and missed collaboration opportunities.
target_user: University students seeking to form or join study groups for their courses.
goals: Enable students to create a profile with courses, availability, and preferred study style
Automatically match students into potential study groups based on shared criteria
Allow students to request to join or create groups
Provide a simple in‑app messaging channel for group communication
Offer a calendar view to schedule group study sessions
Ensure data privacy and operate without paid third‑party services
non_goals: Providing tutoring or content creation services
Integrating paid APIs or external commercial services
Developing a mobile native app (web‑only focus)
requirements: Responsive web application accessible via modern browsers
User registration using university email (or simple email verification)
Profile fields: courses (multiple), weekly availability slots, study style (e.g., silent, collaborative, mixed)
Matching engine that considers course overlap, overlapping availability, and study style compatibility
Group creation, join request workflow, and admin approval within each group
In‑app real‑time chat limited to group members (WebSocket or polling)
Calendar integration to propose and confirm study session times
Secure storage of user data (encrypted at rest)
No reliance on paid third‑party APIs or services
Deployable on a free tier cloud provider (e.g., Heroku, Render, Vercel)

user_stories.i_want: to register using my university email and verify my account
user_stories.so_that: I can securely access the platform and be recognized as a campus member
acceptance_criteria: Registration form accepts email and password
Verification email is sent via free SMTP service
User cannot log in without verifying email
Password must meet minimum complexity rules

user_stories.i_want: to create a profile that lists my courses, weekly availability, and preferred study style
user_stories.so_that: the system can match me with compatible peers
acceptance_criteria: Profile page allows selection of multiple courses from a predefined list
Availability can be entered as recurring time blocks (e.g., Mon 4‑6 pm)
Study style options include Silent, Collaborative, Mixed
Profile data is saved and displayed correctly on edit
Only the owner can edit their profile

user_stories.i_want: to view a list of suggested study groups that match my profile
user_stories.so_that: I can quickly find groups that fit my schedule and learning preferences
acceptance_criteria: Matching algorithm runs daily and updates suggestions
Each suggestion shows group name, shared courses, overlapping availability, and study style match score
Students can filter suggestions by course or time
Clicking a suggestion opens group details

user_stories.i_want: to request to join a suggested group or create my own group
user_stories.so_that: I can either join an existing community or start a new one with peers
acceptance_criteria: Join request button sends a notification to group admin
Group admin can approve or reject requests
Creator can set group name, description, and optional max size
Creator becomes group admin automatically
System prevents duplicate join requests

user_stories.i_want: to chat with my group members inside the app
user_stories.so_that: we can coordinate study topics and share resources in real time
acceptance_criteria: Chat window displays messages in chronological order
Messages are persisted for the duration of the group
Basic markdown (bold, italics) is supported
Only group members can view the chat

user_stories.i_want: to propose and confirm study session times using a shared calendar view
user_stories.so_that: we can schedule meetings that fit everyone’s availability
acceptance_criteria: Calendar shows each member’s available slots
Proposer can suggest a date/time range
Other members can accept or propose alternatives
When all members accept, the session is marked as confirmed
All core functionalities (registration, profile creation, matching, group join/create, chat, calendar scheduling) work on desktop and mobile browsers
No paid third‑party services are used; all external calls rely on free tiers or self‑hosted solutions
User data is stored securely and complies with basic privacy standards
System remains responsive with up to 200 concurrent users (performance target for MVP)
The product can be deployed within a five‑week sprint using a team of four developers

risks.description: Limited time (five weeks) may restrict thorough testing and polishing
University email verification may require SMTP relay that could be throttled
Matching algorithm complexity could exceed the five‑week budget
Real‑time chat implementation without paid services may face scalability limits
Data privacy compliance without legal counsel may expose user data risks
